rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi sketches the sūra’s sequence: seek refuge from sins, begin good works in God’s name, praise and recognize his lordship and mercy, heed judgment, worship and seek help, ask guidance, and avoid ignorance and error.
rows.anchor: بسم الله الرحمان الرحيم } نشرع في أداء كل الخيرات والمأمورات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the Fātiḥa can yield ten thousand useful questions; he wrote the introduction to show that this claim is attainable, despite the scoffing of envious and ignorant opponents.
rows.anchor: يمكن أن يستنبط من فوائدها ونفائسها عشرة آلاف مسألة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking refuge in God means seeking protection from every prohibited act, including sins and wrong beliefs.
rows.anchor: المراد منه الاستعاذة بالله من جميع المنهيات والمحظورات

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Razi cites as a famous prophetic report that the community will divide into seventy-three sects, all in the Fire except one; he says this shows the other seventy-two hold false creeds.
rows.anchor: ستفترق أمتي على ثلاث وسبعين فرقة : كلهم في النار إلا فرقة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each deviant Muslim sect errs across many questions concerning God’s essence, attributes, rulings, acts and names, as well as compulsion, decree, justice, reward, resurrection, promises, threats, legal status and imamate.
rows.anchor: مسائل كثيرة من المباحث المعلقة بذات الله تعالى ،   وبصفاته ،   وبأحكامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the roughly seven hundred deviant sects outside the Muslim community add further errors in rational theology and questions of essences and attributes, all covered by seeking refuge.
rows.anchor: فرق الضلالات من الخارجين عن هذه الأمة يقربون من سبعمائة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prohibited actions include whatever the Qur’an, mass-transmitted or solitary reports, communal consensus, or sound analogy forbids; their number exceeds a thousand and the refuge formula encompasses them all.
rows.anchor: فهي عبارة عن كل ما ورد النهي عنه : إما في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One can seek refuge from something only after knowing it and recognizing its falsehood and ugliness; thus this formula contains thousands of substantial, certain questions.
rows.anchor: الاستعاذة من الشيء لا تمكن إلا بعد معرفة المستعاذ منه

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Razi reports the scholarly convention that God has 1,001 sacred names found in scripture and Sunna, and says inquiry into each name is a noble subject.
rows.anchor: قد اشتهر عند العلماء أن لله تعالى ألفا وواحدا من الأسماء المقدسة المطهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing a divine name presupposes knowing its referent, arguments for the referent’s existence, and answers to objections against it; these inquiries alone exceed a thousand questions.
rows.anchor: العلم بالاسم لا يحصل إلا إذا كان مسبوقا بالعلم بالمسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ is for attachment and governs an implied verb: “In God’s name I begin performing acts of obedience.”
rows.anchor: الباء في قوله { بسم الله } باء الإلصاق ،   وهي متعلقة بفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Understanding the implied beginning requires surveying all obedience: true creeds and sincere deeds, their proofs, and answers to objections, a body of inquiry that may exceed ten thousand questions.
rows.anchor: بعد الوقوف على أقسام الطاعات ،   وهي العقائد الحقة والأعمال الصافية مع الدلائل والبينات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The refuge formula negates improper beliefs and acts, while the basmala affirms what ought to be believed and done; sound reason and clear truth support this order.
rows.anchor: أعوذ بالله } إشارة إلى نفي ما لا ينبغي من العقائد والأعمال ،   وقوله { بسم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise is praise for a blessing, and praise for a blessing requires knowing it; God’s blessings cannot be counted, as the Qur’an says.
rows.anchor: الحمد إنما يكون حمدا على النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rational person should examine the self, composed of soul and body; the body is the less excellent and less beneficial of the two parts.
rows.anchor: العاقل يجب أن يعتبر ذاته ،   وذلك لأنه مؤلف من نفس وبدن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anatomists have identified nearly five thousand benefits and interests that God wisely arranged in the creation of the human body.
rows.anchor: أصحاب التشريح وجدوا قريبا من خمسة آلاف نوع من المنافع والمصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Known bodily benefits are only a drop in the ocean of the unknown; understanding divine wisdom in creating the human being involves ten thousand questions or more.
rows.anchor: نسبة هذا القدر المعلوم المذكور إلى ما لم يعلم وما لم يذكر كالقطرة في البحر المحيط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding the wisdom evident in the Throne, Footstool, heavens, fixed and moving stars, and the varied measures and colors of created things expands the inquiry to roughly a million questions.
rows.anchor: إلى هذه الجملة آثار حكم الله تعالى في تخليق العرش والكرسي وأطباق السماوات ،   وأجرام النيرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same inquiry includes the wisdom in minerals, plants, animals, their kinds and states; God has made most of creation serve human benefit.
rows.anchor: تخليق الأمهات والمولدات من الجمادات والنباتات والحيوانات وأصناف أقسامها وأحوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi links the statement that God subjected what is in the heavens and earth for people to the vast created benefits contained in praise.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى : { وسخر لكم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because all these innumerable blessings and their wisdom fall under praise to God, the phrase “Praise belongs to God” encompasses about a million questions, more or less.
rows.anchor: أن قوله جل جلاله : { الحمد لله } مشتمل على ألف ألف مسألة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Lord” is in a genitive construction with “the worlds” as its genitive complement; understanding this relation requires knowing both terms.
rows.anchor: أن قوله : { رب } مضاف وقوله : { العالمين } مضاف إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One cannot know God as Lord of the worlds without first understanding what “Lord” and “the worlds” mean.
rows.anchor: فمن المحال حصول العلم بكونه تعالى ربا للعالمين إلا بعد معرفة رب والعالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worlds comprise every existent other than God: spatial bodies, incorporeal entities, and attributes; bodies divide into simple entities and composites.
rows.anchor: العالمين عبارة عن كل موجود سوى الله تعالى ،   وهي على ثلاثة أقسام : المتحيزات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi lists spheres, stars and elemental “mothers” among simple bodies, and the three generated kinds—minerals, plants and animals—among composites.
rows.anchor: فهي الأفلاك والكواكب والأمهات ،   وأما المركبات فهي المواليد الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says there is no proof that bodies are limited to the familiar cosmic categories: since an infinite void lies beyond the world and God can do all possible things, He can create countless external worlds, each larger than this one and containing analogous heavens, earths and celestial bodies.
rows.anchor: ثبت بالدليل أنه حصل خارج العالم خلاء لا نهاية له ،   وثبت بالدليل أنه تعالى قادر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects philosophers’ arguments that there is only one world as weak and based on unsound premises; he cites Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī’s verses about God’s many heavens and the smallness of our past and future.
rows.anchor: ودلائل الفلاسفة في إثبات أن العالم واحد دلائل ضعيفة ركيكة مبنية على مقدمات واهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a lifetime devoted to mineral wonders, plants’ flowers and fruits, or the varieties of beasts, wild animals, birds and insects would not reach the depths of these topics.
rows.anchor: لنفد عمره في أقل القليل من هذه المطالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi links the inexhaustibility of created wonders and divine wisdom to the Qur’anic image of earthly trees as pens and seas as ink, which would not exhaust God’s words.
rows.anchor: ولو أن ما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام والبحر يمده من بعده سبعة أبحر ما نفدت كلمات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy means both rescuing people from kinds of affliction and bringing benefits to those in need.
rows.anchor: أن الرحمة عبارة عن التخليص من أنواع الآفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing how God rescues people requires knowing the many afflictions; medical works reveal only some possible diseases in each organ and body part.
rows.anchor: لا يمكن معرفته إلا بعد معرفة أقسام الآفات ،   وهي كثيرة لا يعلمها إلا الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflection on how God guided human minds to identify foods and medicines from minerals, plants and animals opens an ocean of knowledge without shore.
rows.anchor: كيف هدى عقول الخلق إلى معرفة أقسام الأغذية والأدوية من المعادن والنبات والحيوان

rows.speaker: جالينوس
rows.claim: Razi recounts Galen’s story that, while writing about the eye’s benefits, he withheld his account of the divine wisdom in the two hollow optic nerves meeting at one place; an angel in a dream rebuked him, so he wrote the account.
rows.anchor: حكى جالينوس أنه لما صنف كتابه في منافع أعضاء العين قال : بخلت على الناس بذكر حكمة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: جالينوس
rows.claim: Galen said his thickened spleen resisted every treatment he knew; in a vision an angel directed him to bleed the vein between the little and ring fingers, which cured it.
rows.anchor: إن طحالي قد غلظ فعالجته بكل ما عرفت فلم ينفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says many early medical signs trace to promptings and inspirations like Galen’s experiences, and reflection on them shows that divine mercy exceeds measurement and enumeration.
rows.anchor: أكثر علامات الطب في أوائلها تنتهي إلى أمثال هذه التنبيهات والإلهامات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is performing an act that has been commanded, out of reverence for the commander.
rows.anchor: العبادة عبارة عن الإتيان بالفعل المأمور به على سبيل التعظيم للآمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship requires proving that the world has one God, able to do all possible things, knowing all knowable things, and free of need; He commands and forbids, so creatures must obey and submit.
rows.anchor: قادرا على مقدورات لا نهاية لها ،   عالما بمعلومات لا نهاية لها ،   غنيا عن كل الحاجات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To fulfill “You alone we worship,” one must then detail all commands and prohibitions; the religious law books cover the obligations of the present dispensation.
rows.anchor: لابد من تفصيل أقسام تلك التكاليف ،   وبيان أنواع تلك الأوامر والنواهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The obligations encompassed by worship also include those God revealed through earlier prophets and those He assigned to the angels in heaven from their creation.
rows.anchor: تكاليف الله تعالى بحسب الشرائع التي قد كان أنزلها الله تعالى على الأنبياء المتقدمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Legal works explain bodily duties, while duties of the heart are greater, weightier and more elevated; books of ethics and statecraft address them across different religions and peoples.
rows.anchor: أما أقسام التكاليف الموجودة في أعمال القلوب فهي أكبر وأعظم وأجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All these fields of law, worship, ethics and governance fall under “You alone we worship”; the verse contains an ocean of questions that human reason reaches only slightly.
rows.anchor: علم حينئذ أن المسائل التي اشتملت هذه الآية عليها كالبحر المحيط الذي لا تصل العقول والأفكار إلا إلى القليل منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse asks for guidance, which can be attained by seeking knowledge through proof and argument or by purifying the inner self through spiritual discipline.
rows.anchor: أنه عبارة عن طلب الهداية ،   ولتحصيل الهداية طريقان : أحدهما طلب المعرفة بالدليل والحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rational proofs are limitless because every atom in the upper and lower worlds testifies to God’s divinity, might and majestic self-sufficiency; the cited verse says each thing has a sign of His oneness.
rows.anchor: لا ذرة من ذرات العالم الأعلى والأسفل إلا وتلك الذرة شاهدة بكمال إلهيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His proof starts from bodies equal in corporeal essence but different in color, place and condition; corporeality cannot explain this differentiation, so a specifying governor is required.
rows.anchor: أن أجسام العالم متساوية في ماهية الجسمية ،   ومختلفة في الصفات ،   وهي الألوان والأمكنة والأحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the specifying governor is a body, the same argument recurs; if not, the argument reaches its goal. If it acts by nature rather than knowledge and power, differentiation remains unexplained; a living, knowing, powerful agent is required.
rows.anchor: ذلك المخصص إن كان جسما عاد الكلام فيه ،   وإن لم يكن جسما فهو المطلوب

rows.speaker: ضياء الدين عمر
rows.claim: Razi’s father says every individual atom contains infinitely many proofs of divine power, wisdom and mercy: it could occupy infinitely many positions and bear alternate attributes, each possible state showing dependence on its wise, merciful Creator.
rows.anchor: الشيخ الإمام الوالد ضياء الدين عمر رحمه الله يقول : أن لله تعالى في كل جوهر فرد أنواعا غير متناهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thus the rational route to guidance has no end; the alternative route is purification and spiritual discipline, an immense field with a distinct path for each traveler to God.
rows.anchor: أما تحصيل الهداية بطريق الرياضة والتصفية فذلك بحر لا ساحل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says each traveler to God has a distinctive method and path, citing the Qur’anic statement that each has a direction toward which they turn.
rows.anchor: كما قال : { ولكل وجهة هو موليها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intellect cannot master these spiritual secrets or their beginnings; accomplished knowers perceive profound discussions and subtle mysteries that most people’s understanding cannot reach.
rows.anchor: ولا وقوف للعقول على تلك الأسرار ،   ولا خبر عند الأفهام من مبادئ ميادين تلك الأنوار
